Producer review feedback on CG-0MS934XSL00453HF (raised selection feature, currently in_review): when a card raises, the selection highlight does not raise with it. Additionally the raise slider should go to a maximum of 180px with a default of 60px.

Root cause: in HandView.updateSelectionTints(), applySelectionRaise(true) runs BEFORE the tint loop, so on first selection the raise tween starts before the tint overlay exists — the overlay is created at the resting position and is not in the tween targets, so the card raises while the highlight stays behind. Hover pointerover/pointerout also destroy+recreate the overlay, which can orphan it mid-tween.

## Acceptance criteria

1. Regression tests written FIRST (TDD): animated-path first-selection overlay is included in the raise tween targets; hover repaint reuses the overlay in place; reduced-motion first-selection overlay ends at the raised position.
2. The selection highlight overlay always ends at the raised position on first selection (animated and reduced-motion).
3. GymHandPileScene raise slider: RAISE_MAX = 180, RAISE_DEFAULT = 60; reset() restores the default; Controls help text updated.
4. HandView setSelectionLift() API default remains 0 (opt-in) — backward compatible.
5. npm run build succeeds and all HandView + Gym unit tests pass.
data.title: Gym Hand & Pile: selection highlight raises with the card; raise slider max 180 / default 60

## Summary

Research spike to determine the client-side follow-detection mechanism for the "Follow us on Steam" incentive. The Steam client SDK has no direct "user follows this game's store page" call, so candidates must be verified before committing. This feature produces the decision-gate report that F4 depends on.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A report documents and evaluates each candidate: `ISteamFriends::IsFollowing(<developer account>)` (client-side, no backend), Steam Web API `IPlayerService` (game-page follow, needs server + publisher API key), and any other client-side candidates discovered.
- [ ] The report states a recommendation and flags the UX impact of each candidate (e.g. follows developer account vs game page).
- [ ] The recommendation is confirmed with the user (decision gate) and recorded in this item before F4 implementation commits to a mechanism.
- [ ] Any unknown (e.g. whether a server component is acceptable) is surfaced as an open question with options, not silently assumed.

## Minimal Implementation

- Prototype a minimal probe using the Steamworks SDK against a real Steam account (dev environment with Steam running).
- Research Steamworks SDK docs / community reports for `ISteamFriends::IsFollowing` semantics.
- Write findings to the work item as a structured report (markdown), including a decision recommendation.
- No production code committed in this feature.

## Prototype/Experiment

Success = a clear recommendation with evidence (docs/community/experiment) that the implementer can act on without re-research.

## Dependencies

- Parent blocked-by CG-0MSMAD19O0084CAW (Electron launcher) — launcher must exist to run Steamworks in-app.

## Deliverables

- Decision-gate report (in work item comments).
- Confirmed mechanism choice.

# Intake Brief: Electron Runtime Game Plugin Loader (CG-0MTRO7VMI000F3A5)

## Problem Statement

The Electron launcher currently requires a rebuild to add new games — all games are statically imported and registered in `main.ts`. The producer wants a runtime plugin system so that a game can be added to an already-built launcher distribution by dropping in game artifacts and updating a manifest, without rebuilding the launcher itself.

## Users

- **Distribution operator** (primary) — Ships the Electron launcher and wants to add or update games post-build by placing game artifact directories and updating a manifest.
  - *Story:* As a distribution operator, I can drop a game's built artifacts into a `games/` directory and add a manifest entry, so that the launcher picks it up at startup without rebuilding.
- **Engine maintainer** — Ensures dynamically-loaded games are compatible with the core engine version in the launcher.
  - *Story:* As an engine maintainer, I can declare a required `coreEngineVersion` in a game's manifest, so that the launcher rejects incompatible games with a clear error.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **Runtime game discovery** — The Electron renderer reads a `games/manifest.json` from the content directory at startup, discovers each game's scene class, metadata (title, description, thumbnail), and registers it dynamically so it appears in the Game Selector alongside statically-registered games.
- **Core version compatibility check** — Each game declares a `coreEngineVersion` (semver range) in its manifest; the launcher checks compatibility at load time and skips incompatible games with a clear error message in the Game Selector UI.
- **Asset resolution** — Thumbnails and other game-specific assets are resolved relative to the game's artifact location (not relative to the launcher's `public/` directory).
- **Graceful degradation** — If the manifest is missing, malformed, or a game fails to load, the launcher continues with the statically-registered games and logs an error. Incompatible games are hidden from the selector but their presence is noted (e.g., "Incompatible game: X — requires core vY.Z").
- **All related documentation is updated** to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
- **Full project test suite must pass** with the loader present (no regression for build-time presets).

## Constraints

- **Electron-only** — Web runtime plugin is explicitly out of scope.
- **Build-time presets** are handled in CG-0MTR7DLMY008CK17 (the parent epic); this is purely the runtime plugin phase.
- **Backwards compatible** — The existing static game registration (hardcoded imports in `main.ts`) must continue to work; the plugin system augments rather than replaces it.
- **No npm publication** of games — games are distributed as artifact directories (Vite library-mode ESM builds).
- **Shared dependencies** — Phaser and core-engine must be externalized (not bundled into game artifacts) to avoid duplication.

## Existing State

- `main.ts` (renderer entry): Static imports of every game scene + static `GAMES` array + Phaser scene registration. No dynamic loading.
- `electron/main.ts`: Loads the renderer from a resolved content directory. Has a `ContentDirectoryProvider` chain for content resolution (bundled → Steam DLC override), but no game discovery logic.
- `electron/launcher-config.ts` + `content-locator.ts`: Content directory resolution with provider chain. Extensible but game-discovery-aware.
- `src/ui/GameSelectorScene.ts`: Reads `GameEntry[]` from Phaser registry (`REGISTRY_KEY_GAMES`), renders the game selector grid.
- Parent epic CG-0MTR7DLMY008CK17 at `plan_complete` will introduce `configs/<preset>.json` for build-time game selection (F3 feature).

## Desired Change

- **Manifest schema**: Define a `games/manifest.json` format with entries containing `id`, `sceneKey`, `title`, `description`, `thumbnail` (relative path), `coreEngineVersion` (semver range), and `entry` (path to the game's ESM entry point).
- **Manifest loader**: A new module (e.g., `src/ui/GamePluginLoader.ts`) that reads the manifest from the content directory, validates entries, and returns a `GameEntry[]` array that merges with statically-registered games.
- **Version compatibility**: Use a semver range matcher (e.g., `semver.satisfies`) to check `coreEngineVersion` against the launcher's core engine version.
- **Dynamic scene loading**: For each compatible game, use `import()` to load the game's ESM entry point, extract the scene class, and register it with `scene.add(sceneKey, SceneClass)` before booting Phaser.
- **Asset paths**: Thumbnails are loaded from a path relative to the game's artifact directory (e.g., `games/my-game/assets/thumbnail.png`), resolved by the plugin loader.
- **Game Selector integration**: The Game Selector receives the merged list (static + dynamic) and renders them identically. Incompatible games are either hidden or shown with a disabled state and tooltip explaining the incompatibility.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/ui/GamePluginLoader.ts` — **New file.** Reads manifest, validates entries, loads game chunks dynamically, returns merged `GameEntry[]`.
- `src/ui/GameSelectorScene.ts` — Update to accept dynamically-loaded games; add UI for incompatible game indicators.
- `main.ts` — Update `preBoot` callback to call `GamePluginLoader.load()` and merge with static `GAMES`.
- `electron/main.ts` — May need to expose the resolved content directory path to the renderer (e.g., via `preload.cjs` → `window.TCE.contentDir`) so the plugin loader can find the manifest.
- `electron/preload.cjs` — Add preload bridge for `TCE.contentDir` if not already exposed.
- `package.json` — Add `semver` as a dependency (or use a lightweight alternative).
- `docs/DEVELOPER.md` — Document the `games/manifest.json` schema and plugin loading process.
- `AGENTS.md` — Add plugin loading pattern to the Game Architecture Best Practices section.

## Risks & Assumptions

- **Dynamic import() in Electron renderer** — Loading ESM modules dynamically in the Electron renderer (Chromium context) may have path resolution quirks. *Mitigation:* Prototype early; use absolute paths resolved from the manifest's content directory.
- **Shared dependency bundling** — If games bundle their own Phaser/core-engine copies, the result is heavy and may cause class-identity issues (two Phaser instances). *Assumption:* Games are built as Vite library modules with `rollupOptions.external: ['phaser', '@core-engine/*']` so they rely on the launcher's bundled copies.
- **Thumbnail loading** — Electron's `file://` protocol may have CORS restrictions for loading images from `games/*/assets/`. *Mitigation:* Use `fs://` protocol or copy thumbnails to a shared asset location during game registration; or use `nativeImage` API in preload.
- **Scope creep** — Features like hot-reload of plugins, game updates, per-game settings panels, or web runtime support are natural follow-ons but are **out of scope**. *Mitigation:* Document them as linked follow-up opportunities.
- **Assumption:** The `games/` directory lives inside the content directory (resolved by `launcher-config.ts`), e.g., `<contentDir>/games/`.
- **Assumption:** `coreEngineVersion` uses semver ranges (e.g., `"~4.0.0"`) and compatibility is checked via major version (breaking changes) and minor/patch (non-breaking).
- **Assumption:** Games are built with Vite library mode, producing ESM chunks (e.g., `dist/index.js`) that export a `GameScene` class and a `GAME_INFO` object.

## Appendix: Clarifying Questions & Answers

- Q: "Where should the manifest live — in the content directory (`games/manifest.json`) or in Electron's userData (`~/Library/Application Support/TCE/plugins/manifest.json`)?" — Answer (producer, CG-0MTR7DLMY008CK17 planning session): "In the content directory, alongside game artifacts." Source: planning comment on CG-0MTR7DLMY008CK17. Research: content directory is the game content root resolved by `launcher-config.ts`, so placing the manifest there keeps game artifacts and metadata together.
- Q: "Should dynamically-added games declare a required core version?" — Answer (producer, this session): "Yes — core-engine version." Source: existing description note.
- Q: "What happens to incompatible games in the Game Selector?" — Answer (assumption): "Hidden from the selector, with their incompatibility noted in error logs. Future work could add a disabled entry with a tooltip." Source: reasoned assumption from AC4 draft. *OPEN for producer confirmation.*
- Q: "Should the plugin loader run synchronously (blocking Phaser boot) or asynchronously (show a loading state)?" — Answer (assumption): "Asynchronously, with a brief loading overlay if needed. The `GamePluginLoader.load()` returns a Promise that resolves before the `preBoot` callback completes." Source: reasoned assumption for good UX. *OPEN for producer confirmation.*

## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **CG-0MP2988UN009P9LM** – Extract shared HUD layer into core engine and adopt across games (completed)
- **CG-0MTRO7ECL006ID7J** – Integration verification — full build & test suite (blocked)
- **CG-0MQVJ4DIC009K8D8** – Scenario Validation Test (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `docs/DEVELOPER.md` — matched: acceptance, add, added, already, app, artifact, assets, base, behaviour, build, checks, chunks, clear, compatibility, composition, context, core, criteria, decisions, declaration, declare, dep, desired, dir, discovered, disk, distribution, draft, drop, dynamically, electron, engine, entries, error, esm, explicitly, feature, files, follow, game, games, gameselectorscene, generated, green, implement, import, info, injection, item, json, key, launcher, library, load, loader, loads, location, main, may, mode, module, must, need, needs, next, npm, parent, part, path, phase, phaser, plugin, policy, post, present, range, reads, rebuild, registry, regression, relative, required, resolved, review, runtime, scan, scene, scenekey, schema, scope, selector, separately, session, shared, ships, should, show, sibling, skipped, source, specific, src, start, startup, still, sufficient, suite, system, target, test, them, thumbnail, time, true, update, use, version, via, vite, web, yes, you
- `AGENTS.md` — matched: acceptance, add, added, already, app, artifact, assets, base, behaviour, build, checks, compatibility, composition, context, core, criteria, decisions, dep, dir, discovery, drop, electron, engine, error, esm, feature, files, follow, game, games, goal, green, implement, import, info, intake, item, json, key, launcher, load, loads, main, may, mode, module, must, need, needs, next, npm, parent, part, path, phase, phaser, plugin, policy, present, producer, reads, refine, registry, regression, relative, required, resolved, review, runtime, scene, schema, scope, selector, separately, session, shared, should, show, source, specific, src, start, still, sufficient, suite, system, target, test, them, thumbnail, time, true, update, use, version, via, vite, want, web, you

# Intake Brief — Update AGENTS.md for the split multi-repo structure and cross-repo change guidance (CG-0MUMAIIT40002MRP)

## Problem Statement

`AGENTS.md` advertises the split multi-repo topology but still points at game
sources under `example-games/<game>/…` that no longer exist in the core
checkout (only `example-games/gym/` remains), and it gives no guidance on
whether an agent working in the core repo may touch sibling game repos. Agents
therefore either follow stale paths or treat sibling games as out-of-bounds —
blocking the core↔game co-evolution the split was meant to enable.

## Users

- **Engine maintainer / agent working in the core repo (primary)** — needs
  `AGENTS.md` to describe the real topology (merged core + `tce-*` sibling
  repos; each game repo composes the core as a `./core` submodule) and to
  explicitly permit appropriate changes in sibling game repos.
  - *Story:* As an agent working in the core repo, I can make an engine API
    change and update the affected sibling game repo(s), run their tests and
    push them, so core and games do not silently drift.
- **Game developer working in a `tce-<game>` repo** — needs to know the shared
  conventions still apply and how the core is composed; the cross-repo guidance
  makes explicit what the core may change in their repo.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `AGENTS.md` accurately describes the split topology: the core repo (engine +
   Gym + launcher shell + distribution) with game repos as **sibling
   `tce-<game>` checkouts**, each composing the core as a `./core` git
   submodule; the core carries no games at HEAD except the Gym. Wording matches
   `docs/dev/multi-repo-architecture.md` and `README.md`.
2. Cross-repo working guidance is added to the **existing** *Project-specific
   guidance* and *Worklog Rules* sections (option B — no new top-level
   section): an agent working in the core repo may and should make appropriate
   changes in sibling game repos, including editing, running tests, building,
   committing, and pushing to the game repo's `dev` branch (**never `main`**),
   and using that repo's Worklog store when one exists (otherwise recording the
   cross-repo change on the core work item).
3. All stale in-body game paths are corrected to the sibling layout — e.g.
   `example-games/main-street/…` → `../tce-main-street/src/…`,
   `example-games/golf/…` → `../tce-golf/src/…`, plus the `blackjack` and
   `coloretto` references; remaining `example-games/` references are Gym-only.
4. The mandated context-budget artifacts stay consistent: the threshold file is
   refreshed in the same commit (pre-push gate + guard test).
5. All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code
   comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
6. Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- Documentation-only change (issue type `chore`); no code behaviour change.
- `AGENTS.md` is loaded every session and is **size-gated**: keep additions
  concise, and refresh `docs/dev/context-budget.thresholds.json` in the same
  commit (exact-match convention; the guard test fails on drift).
- Follow the doc-update policy; write in UK English.
- Guidance must not weaken safety/gates: pushes still target `dev` only, and
  the build → test → commit order and `wl`-only work-item mutations still hold.
- No new top-level `AGENTS.md` section (operator chose option B).

## Existing State

- `AGENTS.md` already has an opening paragraph, a *Directory Structure* section
  and an *Example Games* component bullet describing the split (core +
  `tce-<game>` siblings, `./core` submodule).
- Six stale non-gym game-path references remain (lines 251, 281, 284, 340,
  346, 469).
- There is no statement that an agent working in core may modify sibling game
  repos (edit/test/push/worklog).
- No sibling game repo currently ships an active Worklog database;
  `../tce-main-street/.worklog/` holds only a leftover `worktrees/` directory
  — so the “if a worklog exists” clause is forward-looking.
- `docs/dev/multi-repo-architecture.md` (merged-core / Option A) and `README.md`
  describe the sibling topology and are the reference for the corrected wording.

## Desired Change

- Tighten the structure prose / *Example Games* bullet to unambiguously state
  the sibling topology and the submodule direction (game → core at `./core`;
  the core never submodules games).
- Add concise cross-repo-change guidance in *Project-specific guidance* and in
  *Worklog Rules / TCE Project Conventions*.
- Correct the six stale game paths to `../tce-<game>/src/…`.
- Refresh `docs/dev/context-budget.thresholds.json`.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `AGENTS.md` — structure description, cross-repo guidance, stale-path fixes.
- `docs/dev/context-budget.thresholds.json` — regenerated threshold (mandatory
  same-commit refresh).
- `docs/dev/multi-repo-architecture.md` — reference only; align wording only if
  a contradiction is found (no change expected).
- `README.md` — consistency check; fix only if the `AGENTS.md` change exposes a contradiction.
- `docs/DEVELOPER.md` — consistency check; fix only if the `AGENTS.md` change exposes a contradiction.
- `scripts/refresh-context-thresholds.sh` — context-budget refresh/check script backing the pre-push gate (AC4).
- `tests/scripts/context-budget-thresholds.test.ts` — guard test for the committed thresholds (runs in the unit profile) (AC4).
- `.githooks/pre-push` — pre-push gate enforcing the context-budget thresholds (AC4).
- `package.json` — `context:check` / `context:refresh` npm script entries for the gate (AC4).

## Related Work

- **Potentially related work items:**
  - `REFACTOR: break out core engine and individual games into their own projects. (CG-0MTR7DLMY008CK17)` — open, `plan_complete` — parent epic; this item contributes to its docs AC.
  - `Documentation for multi-repo workflow (CG-0MTRO7BFQ003IN2X)` — completed (F6) — the original multi-repo doc update, including `AGENTS.md`.
  - `Merge the core into Tableau-Card-Engine (Option A): games compose it as ./core, distribution composes siblings (CG-0MUJ0IAJM009X0Q2)` — completed — established the merged-core topology this brief documents.
  - `Write the Option A decision record and update the multi-repo architecture docs (CG-0MUJ0IJ6300398VR)` — completed.
  - `AGENTS.md exceeds context-budget threshold, blocking all pushes to dev (CG-0MUFCL5N50023PHJ)` / `[infra] context-budget pre-push gate… (CG-0MTCRF0K2006N0HR)` — completed — the gate that constrains this change.
- **Potentially related docs (paths):**
  - `docs/dev/multi-repo-architecture.md` — merged-core sibling topology.
  - `docs/dev/merged-core-decision.md`, `docs/dev/per-game-src-layout-decision.md` — layout decisions.
  - `docs/DEVELOPER.md` — multi-repo workflow, aliases, per-game dev loop.
  - `README.md` — repo map and sibling clone commands.
  - `docs/dev/context-budget.md` — threshold refresh workflow.

## Risks & Assumptions

- **Assumption:** the “working in core may change sibling games” permission is
  additive to the global *Repository Boundaries* discipline, which targets
  `.pi/`/`skill/`/agent-infrastructure — not sibling product repos.
- **Risk — context-budget gate:** growing `AGENTS.md` without refreshing the
  threshold blocks all pushes. *Mitigation:* concise edits + same-commit
  threshold refresh; verify with `scripts/refresh-context-thresholds.sh --check`.
- **Risk — missed stale path:** the sweep may miss a reference (e.g. a
  future-added game). *Mitigation:* verification `grep -n 'example-games/' AGENTS.md`
  must return Gym/structure entries only.
- **Risk — over-broad reading:** cross-repo guidance could be misread as licence
  to push to `main` or skip tests. *Mitigation:* explicitly restate `dev`-only
  pushes and test-before-push in the same paragraph.
- **Scope-creep risk:** rewriting the whole multi-repo docs set is out of
  scope; record further gaps as linked work items rather than expanding this
  one.
- **Assumption:** no new top-level `AGENTS.md` section (operator chose option B).

## Appendix: Clarifying Questions & Answers

- Q: “Where should the cross-repo changes guidance live in `AGENTS.md`?” —
  Answer (producer, this session): “(B) Fold into the existing
  *Project-specific guidance* + *Worklog Rules* sections only.” Source:
  interactive reply. Research: enumerated `AGENTS.md` section headings and
  confirmed *Project-specific guidance* and *Worklog Rules / TCE Project
  Conventions* as the natural hosts.
- Q: “Should the same change fix the now-stale in-body game paths?” — Answer
  (producer, this session): “yes.” Source: interactive reply. Research:
  `grep -n 'example-games/' AGENTS.md` found six non-gym references (lines 251,
  281, 284, 340, 346, 469); confirmed the sibling targets exist in
  `../tce-<game>/src/…` (e.g. `../tce-main-street/src/scenes/MainStreetOverlayContent.ts`).
- Q (producer freeform note): “this includes allowing test and push in
  individual project repos, as well as working with worklog if it exists in
  that repo.” — Recorded as scope for AC2. Evidence: a sibling survey found no
  active Worklog database; `../tce-main-street/.worklog/` holds only
  `worktrees/`.

## Foundational Test-References

- `scripts/refresh-context-thresholds.sh --check` — context-budget threshold consistency (AC4).
- `grep -n 'example-games/' AGENTS.md` — stale-path sweep (AC3).
- Doc/lint checks in the unit profile (e.g. `.pi`/docs guard tests where present) — no behavioural tests change for a docs-only edit.
- Full suite (`npm test` / `npm run build`) — release gate per quality gates.

## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **CG-0MTRO6P18003AZIZ** – Design architecture & extraction script with history (completed)
- **CG-0MQL8A0CH0017SK1** – Core Engine Checkpoint Unit Tests (completed)
- **CG-0MP12U37I009PWPQ** – Review DEVELOPER.md (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `docs/DEVELOPER.md` — matched: agents, change, changes, clear, core (+20 more)
- `AGENTS.md` — matched: agents, appropriate, change, changes, core (+16 more)
- `CHANGELOG.md` — matched: agents, change, changes, clear, core (+16 more)

data.comment: question: Audit follow-up — would a GitHub CI gate make this audit pass? Analysis: no, not by itself. The context-budget gate AC4 references already exists in this repo (pre-push hook .githooks/pre-push; guard test tests/scripts/context-budget-thresholds.test.ts, which runs in the unit profile the audit executed green; and npm run context:check, which passes). AC4 was marked 'partial' by Phase 1 only because the screening manifest is built from the item's five Key Files (AGENTS.md, docs/dev/context-budget.thresholds.json, docs/dev/multi-repo-architecture.md, README.md, docs/DEVELOPER.md) plus a coarse repo index — the gate/guard files were never in scope and could not be cited.
